title: the push guard reads the words bash builds as written: ANSI-C and locale quoting, substitutions inside a word, expansions bash makes nothing of, braces, and a comment or arithmetic the scan misreads
status: fixed after 0.5.0: the guard reads each word as bash may build it, its quotings decoded, each substitution a hole in its word, every variable unset and every substitution empty, its braces expanded, and a lone GIT_DIR=x as one that may name the repository (DESIGN.md, 13)
world: memory; the git world runs it over real git (build step 6)

steps.note: each guard step is one of the guard grammar's commands, so the guard's answer is also judged by git's recorded one: bash decodes $'pu\x73h' to push and runs git push origin main; under the mutant that reads a $'...' as a $ and a quoted span, as the guard did until the fix, the verb is $pu\x73h, the push passes and G11a is red here
the same quoting around the string env's -S splits: read as a $ and a quoted span, the string is the variable $git push origin main, and env splits nothing

bash reads $"main" as the double-quoted main where no message catalog translates it; under the mutant that reads it as a $ and a quoted span the name is $main, a variable whole, whose value the guard cannot know, and the push to main passes

bash runs true, which prints nothing, and builds the verb push; under the mutant that reads no command's own text with its substitutions as holes, the whole reading cuts the word at the substitution's parentheses and the push passes
the verb is a substitution whole that prints push; under the mutant that reads a word bash builds only as its text, the verb is not push and the push passes
the command is a substitution whole that prints git's path; under the same mutant the command is not git and the push passes
where NOPE is not set bash drops the word $NOPE and runs git push origin main; under the mutant that reads no word unset, $NOPE is the command and the push passes
brace expansion makes push and an empty word, which bash drops; under the mutant that expands no braces the verb is {push,} and the push passes
bash builds the option -f, a plain force; under the mutant that refuses no option whose name bash builds, the word is no option the guard knows and the forced push passes
bash builds the name main; under the mutant that refuses no name bash may build into the default or the board branch, the push to main passes

bash takes the line continuation out before it reads on, so the # after echo's blank opens a comment and the apostrophe in it opens nothing: git push origin main runs; under the mutant that reads a word's start as ended by a continuation, the apostrophe opens a quote to the last line and the push passes

b fetches in its second clone, b-other, makes a claim commit naming itself there, and runs GIT_DIR=<the clones>/b/.git; git -C ../b-other push --force-with-lease origin claude/1 from its session's clone, which never fetched claude/1: the assignment sets the shell's variable, which git sees only where GIT_DIR was exported before, so git may take the lease in b-other, and the guard, judging the push there too, refuses it; under the mutant that reads a lone assignment as naming the repository for good, the push is judged in b's own clone alone, the lease is taken and G11a and G1 are red here

the same lease by git -C ../b-other, onto claude/$'1', which bash decodes to claude/1: under the mutant that reads a $'...' as a $ and a quoted span the name is claude/$1, which no claim file is read for, and the lease is taken

b's lease from its own clone, between cat <<E$(echo x)F with a body Don't and cat <<'EOF' with a body It's: bash reads the delimiter word whole, E$(echo x)F, expanding nothing in it, so the first body ends at the line E$(echo x)F and the push runs; under the mutant that cuts the delimiter at the substitution's (, the delimiter is E$, no line ends the body, the push is read as part of it and the two apostrophes pair around it, and the lease is taken
